    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Draymond Green rarely, if ever, refuses an opportunity to jab back at his critics.

    Following the Golden State Warriors' 88-87 win over the Boston Celtics on Sunday, the veteran forward had plenty to say to those who believe he's not carrying enough of the scoring burden with Stephen Curry sidelined due to an abdominal tear.

    In a recent development, green scored 9 points in the Warriors' win, his highest total of the season thus far. But scoring more has never been his role and he doesn't intend to change that, even with the team's top scorer out.

    In a recent development, "I'm never going to, in Year 15, be like 'Oh, man, Steph's out — it's my chance,'" Green told reporters, via The Athletic's Jason Jones. "When I was in Year 6, it was my chance, and I would do what I do.

    "But Year 15? That would never be my mindset," he added. "As someone who can do a multitude of things on the basketball court, I would never deduce myself down to you gotta go score.".

    It has been revealed that all nine of Green's points on Sunday came in the first quarter when he hit three 3-pointers. Green said after the game that Warriors coach Steve Kerr told him to look to shoot from the corner. That helped Golden State run out to a 27-22 lead after the opening 12 minutes of play.

    The Celtics went ahead with a third-quarter surge, leading by 11 at one point. But the Warriors tightened up on defense, allowing them to chip away at the second-half deficit. Golden State finally took an 88-86 lead with 2:38 remaining in regulation on a 3-pointer from Brandin Podziemski.

    On Boston's final possession, Green prevented Jayson Tatum from driving to the basket and forced him to take a fadeaway jumper. But the 16-footer missed and the Warriors got their ninth win of the season.

    Tatum was held to 4 points in the second half with Green defending him. That's exactly what Golden State needs Green to do, according to Kerr. Green offered to come off the bench if it would help the team, but Kerr said his defense is too valuable throughout the game.

    "I told him I had no desire to bring him on the bench because we've got to dig this thing out with defense," Kerr stated, via The Athletic. "And he remains one of the great defenders in the league. He indicated that tonight.".

    It has been revealed that green is averaging 3.6 points in 14 games this season. If that continues, it would be his lowest scoring average since his rookie campaign in 2012-13. He's also grabbing 4.8 rebounds and dishing out 6.3 assists while shooting 33% on 21 3-point attempts.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Etihad Guest, the loyalty program of Abu Dhabi-based Etihad Airways, is expanding its U.S. presence by introducing two new credit cards. Most people won’t get much value from these cards, but they can make sense for Etihad frequent flyers who want elite status.

    Recent findings suggest that the two cards are the Etihad Guest Visa Signature® Card ($99 annual fee) and the Etihad Guest Premier Visa Signature® Card ($499 annual fee). Issued by the First National Bank of Omaha, both offer faster pathways to earning and maintaining elite status and the ability to earn extra miles on Etihad purchases.

    They also offer extra miles on international transactions (neither has foreign transaction fees) and purchases with Etihad’s partner airlines, which include U.S. carriers like American Airlines and JetBlue Airways.

    Here’s what you need to know about the cards.

    The Etihad Guest Visa Signature® Card comes with a $99 annual fee, and it earns Etihad Guest miles at the following rates:.

    3 miles per $1 spent on Etihad purchases.

    2 miles per $1 spent on Etihad partner airline purchases.

    According to recent reports, 2 miles per $1 spent on non-U.S. purchases.

    1 mile per $1 spent on all other U.S. purchases.

    Welcome offer: Through Feb. 3, 2027, the card is offering the following welcome offer for fresh applicants: Earn up to 40,000 welcome Etihad Guest Miles, including 10,000 miles after the first purchase and an additional 30,000 miles after spending $3,000 within the first three billing cycles after account opening.

    Elite status benefits: You’ll also get Etihad Silver status after your first Etihad purchase within 90 days of opening your account. Unlike most airlines, that entry-level status is enough to get you into the business class lounge when traveling through Etihad’s hub at Abu Dhabi’s Zayed International Airport.

    You can retain that status by spending $20,000 a year on the card, or $3,000 a year on Etihad purchases.

    The Etihad Guest Premier Visa Signature® Card comes with a $499 annual fee, and it earns Etihad Guest miles at the following rates:.

    5 miles per $1 spent on Etihad purchases.

    3 miles per $1 spent on Etihad partner airline purchases.

    According to recent reports, 2 miles per $1 spent on non-U.S. purchases.

    1 mile per $1 spent on all other U.S. purchases.

    The only differences in rewards between the premium and standard cards are increased earning rates for eligible airline purchases.

    According to recent reports, welcome offer: Through Feb. 3, 2027, the premium card offers a higher welcome offer compared to the standard card: Earn up to 60,000 welcome Etihad Guest Miles, including 20,000 miles after the first purchase and 40,000 miles after spending $7,000 within the first three billing cycles after account opening.

    Elite status benefits: The premium card offers a faster track to elite status: automatic Silver status upon card approval and Gold status after your first Etihad purchase within 90 days of opening your account.

    It has been revealed that to maintain Gold status, you’ll need to spend $40,000 a year on the card, or $8,000 on Etihad purchases. Otherwise, you’ll have Silver status.

    Wi-Fi benefit: After your first Etihad purchase, you’ll get 3,000 Etihad Guest miles, enough to cover Wi-Fi costs on a long-haul Etihad flight. You’ll then get those miles again after each cardholder anniversary.

    Sources indicate that travel benefits: The card offers a statement credit for Global Entry or TSA PreCheck and select travel protections. If you already have a premium travel card, you might already have access to these perks.

    It has been revealed that the card also includes a Priority Pass lounge access membership. However, an Etihad spokesperson told NerdWallet that it’s the entry-level membership tier, so you’ll need to pay for yourself and guests each time you visit a Priority Pass lounge. Most premium credit cards in the U.S. that offer Priority Pass allow complimentary visits for at least the cardholder.

    The Etihad cards make the most sense for Etihad’s frequent flyers who are flying to or connecting through Abu Dhabi several times a year.

    That’s because the standard card’s accelerated pathway to Etihad Guest’s Silver status tier can unlock the ability to choose business class lounge access in Abu Dhabi as a status perk.

    With the premium card, you get a fast track to Gold. If you select lounge access as a Gold status perk, you can not only bring a guest on the same flight into the lounge, but also access Etihad’s worldwide lounge network. That includes Etihad’s own lounges in New York and Washington, D.C., as well as most partner lounges at other Etihad destinations.

    Bear in mind that while Etihad has many partnerships with other airlines, it’s not part of an alliance, so you don’t get lounge benefits when traveling on partners. You’ll need to be flying on an Etihad-operated flight to get into the lounge.

    If you primarily fly with other carriers, then Etihad status will have limited upside for you.

    However, the Priority Pass lounge membership that comes with the premium card does not have that restriction. You can access Priority Pass lounges while flying on any airline, although you’ll need to pay an additional per-person $35 fee each visit.

    Industry observers note that the earning rates on the Etihad cards are lackluster for everyday spenders. The bonus categories are for airline purchases with Etihad and its partners, as well as international spending.

    That means your day-to-day purchases at home, like groceries, dining out and gas, earn only 1 mile per $1 spent.

    Plus, there are more ways to earn Etihad Guest miles than spending on an Etihad credit card. For example, you can transfer points to Etihad Guest from Bilt Rewards, Capital One and Citi ThankYou.

    Those programs offer cards that typically have better benefits and bonus categories, and they offer flexibility on how you can use your points and miles. With an Etihad card, you can only earn Etihad Guest miles, which expire after 18 months without qualifying flight activity. (If you’re not traveling on Etihad or its partners at least once every 18 months, then you definitely should not get the cards.).

    One of the most interesting perks of the latest cards is the bonus category for spending with Etihad partner airlines — 2 miles per $1 for the standard card and 3 miles per $1 for the premium version. Typically, airline credit cards reward customers only for spending on the airline, not partners.

    There are better cards available, though. Some offer as many or even more points per $1 on flights purchased directly from airlines.

    If you want the card solely to earn more Etihad Guest miles, then the answer for most people is no.

    While you can earn more miles for purchases with Etihad and partner airlines, the earning rates aren’t attractive enough to justify the annual fees, especially when compared with existing cards with currencies that transfer to Etihad Guest.

    Status chasers could benefit from the fast track to elite status — but you would need to be a fairly frequent Etihad flyer to really take advantage of your elite benefits.

    • Robinhood shares were down around 8% in pre-market trading on Wednesday as investors digested weaker-than-expected third-quarter earnings despite growth in options trading and prediction markets.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Robinhood shares were down around 8% in pre-market trading on Wednesday as investors digested weaker-than-expected third-quarter earnings despite growth in options trading and prediction markets.

    Here's how the brokerage performed in its quarter ended Sept. 30, compared with Wall Street estimates, based on a survey of analysts by LSEG:.

    According to recent reports, robinhood's net income fell to $468 million, or 51 cents per share, from $556 million, or 61 cents per share, a year ago. Revenue represented a 12% increase from $1.27 billion in the same quarter last year.

    Despite that gain, transaction-based revenue of $867 million came in below Wall Street estimates from StreetAccount of $879 million, putting focus on whether Robinhood can sustain momentum across its trading businesses and reduce its reliance on volatile market activity.

    Robinhood has been diversifying its business as it tries to expand its brokerage app into a broader financial services platform. Options trading and event contracts have become increasingly key sources of transaction revenue, while the tech giant has continued to invest in wealth management, subscriptions and other offerings.

    According to recent reports, transaction-based revenue grew 19% from the same period last year to $867 million, driven primarily by a more than 500% increase in event contracts revenue. Additionally, options revenue grew 31% to $399 million and equities revenue rose 41% to $121 million.

    Those gains were partially offset by cryptocurrency revenue, which fell 55% to $120 million.

    Chief Financial Officer Shiv Verma told CNBC event contracts on crypto movements did well in the quarter, offering investors another way to express a view on crypto despite the slump in prices and spot trading.

    According to recent reports, net deposits on the Robinhood platform totaled $15.7 billion for the quarter, equal to a 17% annualized growth rate based on total platform assets at the end of Q2 2026. Over the past year, net deposits totaled $71 billion, representing 21% growth compared with total platform assets at the end of Q3 2025.

    —With reporting from CNBC's Robert Hum and Kate Rooney.

    What Is a Reconditioning Fee on a Used Car?

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (718 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nerdwallet

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, A reconditioning fee is an added dealer charge you might find when buying a used car.
    • The reconditioning process varies between dealerships, but typically includes these steps:.
    • Industry observers note that A visual exterior inspection.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, A reconditioning fee is an added dealer charge you might find when buying a used car. It’s intended to cover any costs the dealer incurs to make sure a used car is showroom-ready, from mechanical inspections to detailing.

    The reconditioning process varies between dealerships, but typically includes these steps:.

    Industry observers note that A visual exterior inspection. An auto tech does a quick walk-around the vehicle and notes any corrosion, damage or wear.

    An interior inspection. The engine and auto interior are examined and tested, and any issues are documented.

    A test drive. The car is taken out for a drive to check that it runs well and that the radio, brakes, A/C and other components are all functioning properly.

    Recent findings suggest that service and repair. Any interior or exterior mechanical, functional or cosmetic issues that were found are repaired, including paint, dents, oil changes and major engine work.

    Inspection. Once repairs are completed, the car is inspected again to make sure everything looks and functions as it should.

    In a recent development, detailing. This includes deep interior, engine and exterior cleaning as well as any necessary leather refurbishing, bumper repair or wheel restoration.

    According to recent reports, reconditioning fees are legal, but that doesn’t mean you have to pay them. Dealers can charge whatever they want for a reconditioning fee, and it’s not uncommon to find them ranging from around $500 to over $2,000.

    Sources indicate that the good news: Reconditioning fees, like most dealer extras, can be negotiable. Ask the dealer for a breakdown of the reconditioning fee to see what kind of work was done to prepare the car for sale. If the work was minor but the fee is high — for example, if they’re asking for $1,995 but replaced the floor mats only — that’s a good sign it’s a bogus charge.

    According to recent reports, however, when it comes time for negotiation, don’t just haggle over the reconditioning fee or other individual fees. The best way to negotiate is to focus on the out-the-door price, or the total amount you’re paying for the car. This simplifies the negotiation process and keeps you focused on the true price of your car.

    All dealers invest some amount in reconditioning, but those costs are often built into the dealer’s asking price for a vehicle, rather than as a separate charge.

    Some dealers opt to add a reconditioning fee to the bill because it allows them to advertise a lower asking price online, which doesn’t include fees. It’s a tactic to get you into their dealership, since the asking price is lower than that of other dealerships.

    However, once you arrive, you may find that the out-the-door price is the same — or more — compared with what other dealers are asking.

    Some car-buying experts recommend avoiding dealerships that charge reconditioning fees altogether. But remember that the out-the-door price is what matters at the end of the day, so it’s worth comparing prices at multiple dealerships to find the best deal.

    Reddit is an online forum where people share their thoughts in “threads” on various topics. The popular site includes plenty of discussion on financial subjects like car buying, so we sifted through Reddit threads to get a sense of how users feel about reconditioning fees. People post anonymously, so we cannot confirm their individual experiences or circumstances.

    Industry observers note that reddit users are generally skeptical toward reconditioning fees. Many users view these fees as a bait-and-switch tactic: dealers advertise an attractive price online and then tack on the fee at the dealership, inflating the actual out-the-door cost well above what was listed. Car buyers frequently share stories of being hit with reconditioning fees ranging from a few hundred dollars up to $2,000 or more, often with little or no evidence of what work was actually done.

    According to recent reports, car-buying experts on Reddit point out that most dealerships already build reconditioning costs into the sticker price, so if the fee is listed separately, the dealership may be double-dipping. Several users suggest that car buyers ask their dealer for an itemized breakdown of the work done, but most users recommend negotiating the total out-the-door price rather than individual fees.

    📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1029 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Nerdwallet ↗ Open Full Page

    What Are Repositioning Cruises?

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1029 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nerdwallet

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • A repositioning cruise is a one-way sailing that moves a ship from one region to another.
    • Repositioning cruises are most common in spring (roughly March to May) and fall (roughly September to November), though they can occur at other times of year.
    • Because ships are crossing oceans, these trips often include many days at sea.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    A repositioning cruise is a one-way sailing that moves a ship from one region to another. For example, many ships sail in the Mediterranean Sea during the summer and move to the Caribbean Sea for the winter, and that trip between the two is a repositioning cruise.

    Repositioning cruises are most common in spring (roughly March to May) and fall (roughly September to November), though they can occur at other times of year.

    Because ships are crossing oceans, these trips often include many days at sea. For some travelers, that’s a chance to relax and enjoy the ship’s onboard amenities. Sometimes, these sailings can also be cheaper than traditional cruises.

    Industry observers note that one key consideration for a repositioning cruise is that the embarkation and disembarkation ports will be different. This means you generally can’t buy a standard round-trip flight to and from the same city. Instead, you’ll need transportation to where the cruise starts and another way home from where it ends, which usually means two one-way flights (or one open-jaw ticket) unless you live near one of the ports. While these one-way sailings may be more affordable than traditional cruises, airfare costs may be higher.

    This could be a great opportunity to redeem miles for your flight.

    Another feature that sets these cruises apart is that stops along the way tend to include ports that aren’t traditionally part of regular itineraries. These might include islands like Bermuda, the Azores or the Canary Islands, and on some northern routes, Greenland.

    Just keep in mind that the main purpose of these sailings is to get to a newly introduced region for the next season’s itineraries rather than make daily port stops. So if you’re someone who wants to visit as many places as possible on a cruise, a repositioning sailing may not be the ideal choice.

    Repositioning cruises are often longer than standard cruises, commonly running two to three weeks compared with about a week for a typical sailing, which may appeal to travelers looking for an extended vacation. The experience is often more relaxed, with many days at sea and less of a rush to book shore excursions or visit key sites when off the ship.

    Industry observers note that if there are particular ships with certain amenities — like tattoo parlors or massive waterparks — that you really want to experience, keep in mind that not all ships reposition between regions. Some stay in certain regions year-round.

    For ships that do change locations for the season, there are plenty of onboard activities to fill the time. You can enjoy highlights, food and wine tastings, organized activities and time at the spa, pool or casino.

    Many repositioning crossings are relatively smooth, and modern ships use stabilizers to reduce movement. But since these itineraries cross open ocean rather than staying closer to land, there can be more motion, especially on North Atlantic crossings in fall and winter.

    According to recent reports, if you tend to get seasick, this could be a dealbreaker. Even if a repositioning sailing is smooth, temperatures can be chilly on the open ocean, especially on northerly or spring and fall transatlantic routes, with strong winds that may make suntanning by the pool less appealing.

    You can book one of these sailings in the same way you would book a traditional cruise. But if you’re searching for dates and itineraries on a cruise line’s website, they may be listed as transatlantic, transpacific or Panama Canal sailings rather than repositioning cruises, though some lines do use the term "repositioning." There’s even a website that specializes in rounding up these cruises: RepoCruises.com.

    Keep an eye out for themed sailings that focus on topics like wine, theater or music, where fellow guests on the ship may share similar interests. Cruise lines often schedule them on repositioning cruises to spur demand.

    Here are some repositioning cruises for 2027. They often take place during shoulder seasons, between the most popular cruising times in places like the Mediterranean or Caribbean.

    This journey repositions the ship from Miami, where it sails on Caribbean itineraries, to Seattle, where it will visit ports in Alaska during the spring and summer months.     Regent Seven Seas Cruises' all-suite luxury ship Seven Seas Mariner will sail between Upcoming York and Lisbon, making stops in Canada, Morocco and the Portuguese islands of Madeira and the Azores.

    Departing April 29, 2027, the 16-night journey ends in Lisbon, Portugal, as the ship repositions to Europe, where it will sail various itineraries, including Mediterranean sailings later in the summer season.

    Industry observers note that departing Seattle on Sept. 28, 2027, Norwegian Jade will sail to Yokohama, Japan, with stops in Alaska and northern Japan. This is a way to travel across the Pacific with less jet lag, since the journey takes place over several days, with ship clocks typically adjusted gradually (often an hour at a time) during the sailing. Note that the voyage also crosses the International Date Line.

    Sources indicate that if Greenland has been on your bucket list, this 16-night sailing is a way to get up close and personal with its natural scenery.     💡 Key Takeaways
    • Applied Digital (APLD +20.28%) shares jumped as much as 31% on Monday after the manufacturer said it signed a new 150-megawatt, 18-year lease with a "tier-one investment-grade hyperscaler." The company said the lease brings its contracted base-term revenue above $41 billion.
    • Recent findings suggest that the jump came one trading day after Applied Digital hit its lowest close of the past year, $11.49 on Friday.
    • Applied Digital builds data centers and rents them to companies that need power and space for artificial intelligence computing.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Jonathan Ponciano – Nov 23, 2026 at 6:37PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Applied Digital ›.

    Applied Digital (APLD +20.28%) shares jumped as much as 31% on Monday after the manufacturer said it signed a new 150-megawatt, 18-year lease with a "tier-one investment-grade hyperscaler." The company said the lease brings its contracted base-term revenue above $41 billion. The stock ultimately gave back some of that gain but still closed up 20% at $13.82.

    Recent findings suggest that the jump came one trading day after Applied Digital hit its lowest close of the past year, $11.49 on Friday. Even after Monday's gain, the stock sits 72% below its 52-week high of $49.65 on May 28, and it's down 44% this year.

    Applied Digital builds data centers and rents them to companies that need power and space for artificial intelligence computing. A lease of this kind is a promise of rent once a building is finished and handed over.

    According to recent reports, the organization's quarterly report filed Oct. 7, before Monday's lease, listed $35.7 billion in minimum contracted lease payments. Of that, $468 million is due through May 2027, the end of the company's fiscal year. Payments rise to $1.58 billion the following year and $2.36 billion the year after. Another $26.6 billion is due after May 2031.

    It has been revealed that the reason is largely construction. As of the 10-Q's filing, Applied Digital had 250 megawatts of AI data center capacity running at its Polaris Forge 1 campus in Ellendale, North Dakota, out of 1,410 megawatts under contract. Its other buildings are scheduled to come online between late 2026 and 2028. A 210-megawatt building leased in June to another investment-grade hyperscaler isn't due until the first half of 2028.

    The firm's annual report spells out what happens if building falls behind schedule: "Under certain circumstances, lessees may have the right to terminate applicable leases if there are significant delays in construction." It adds that Applied Digital "may not be able to release the applicable data center in a timely or profitable manner.".

    In a recent development, the tech giant's debt terms already account for that possibility. Under the terms of the 7% notes due 2031, issued by an Applied Digital subsidiary, if that subsidiary receives certain termination fees from a tenant, it generally must use them to pay off the notes, with exceptions if a replacement tenant is found.

    The construction boom is happening as the firm loads up with debt. Applied Digital's long-term debt rose to $6.26 billion at Aug. 31 from $4.96 billion three months earlier. Interest expense for the quarter was $77.4 million, up from $8 million a year before. Meanwhile, revenue grew to $341.9 million from $80.9 million, but the firm posted an operating loss of $62.4 million. It ended the quarter with $2.95 billion in cash.

    This combination is common for data center stocks in a building phase, but it also means the tech giant has little room for delays, since late buildings both push back revenue and give tenants a possible way out.

    The newly introduced lease adds another investment-grade tenant, and its 18-year term is longer than the roughly 15-year term on the June lease, but the risk lies in execution. Applied Digital has to finish several large buildings on schedule, keep financing them, and hand them over before tenants' patience runs out.

    According to recent reports, the tenants' own spending is a second question. In a commentary published Monday, LPL Financial Chief Equity Strategist Jeffrey Buchbinder noted that the six largest U.S. hyperscalers are expected to generate negative free cash flow in 2026 and 2027, based on Bloomberg estimates. He also wrote that political headwinds will likely slow data center construction, "though probably not until 2028," and that rising financing costs could hurt project feasibility. Several of Applied Digital's buildings are due that year.

    It has been revealed that for investors weighing AI stocks tied to the build-out, Applied Digital's next quarterly report should show whether its 2027 construction targets are still on track. Until most of that capacity is in operation, the $41 billion figure reflects the rent the firm expects to collect if construction stays on schedule.

    #153885. Breaking: Ground Truth: The Unsung Foundation Of Industrial Autonomy

    📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (944 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Forbes ↗ Open Full Page

    Breaking: Ground Truth: The Unsung Foundation Of Industrial Autonomy

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (944 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Forbes

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Ronald Bisio is Group President, Field Systems, at Trimble.
    • ​While the public’s attention is captivated by self-driving vehicles, city robotaxis and visions of flying cars, there’s a more consequential autonomous evolution taking place across heavy industry.
    • In building and infrastructure construction, autonomy is a navigation and execution challenge.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Ronald Bisio is Group President, Field Systems, at Trimble.

    ​While the public’s attention is captivated by self-driving vehicles, city robotaxis and visions of flying cars, there’s a more consequential autonomous evolution taking place across heavy industry.

    In building and infrastructure construction, autonomy is a navigation and execution challenge. A 50-ton excavator doesn’t just travel across a construction site from Point A to Point B. It digs trenches, grades slopes and moves thousands of tons of earth to match a complex 3D digital model down to the centimeter. A commercial freight truck hauling 80,000 pounds along a highway corridor isn’t just following traffic. With advanced digital mapping and precise positioning technologies, the truck holds a precise spatial line through torrential rain, dense fog or featureless stretches of road where cameras lose contrast.

    ​In the physical world, knowing what’s immediately around a machine is critical, but a real breakthrough happens when we connect local perception through cameras, LiDAR and radar to spatial ground truth, an invisible infrastructure that complements onboard sensors. This is the high-precision global positioning that uses an absolute coordinate frame of latitude, longitude, elevation and time down to the centimeter. When we connect local perception with precise positioning, we close the gap between machinery observing what’s around and knowing exactly where the machinery sits on the physical earth.

    Industry observers note that with these technological advances in heavy industry, there’s an understandable anxiety about automation replacing human workers. But as I visit customers and jobsites, I see the opposite. Across construction and transportation, the shortage of skilled workers is evident. Contractors can’t find enough experienced workers to meet infrastructure construction demands, and fleet owners are facing historically high driver turnover.

    Sources indicate that ​Fundamentally, industrial autonomy is about elevating human activity and decision making. By putting high-precision digital guidance into a cab, an inexperienced operator can perform complex grading work. Instead of performing repetitive manual layout, workers can oversee connected equipment, manage exceptions and focus on site safety. Autonomous equipment and robotics help automate repetitive and hazardous operations, freeing human talent to focus on higher-order tasks.

    ​Over the past few years, perception sensors have improved dramatically. Cameras, LiDAR and radar give machines exceptional eye-level vision so they can recognize nearby obstacles, workers and vehicles.

    ​But vision sensors have two inherent vulnerabilities. First, these optical systems may degrade in harsh environments and be rendered momentarily blind by factors like heavy dust, glare or dark tunnels. Second, vision sensors lack global context. A camera can spot an obstacle five feet away, but it can’t tell a bulldozer where it sits on the earth’s surface.​.

    To address this, machines may rely on satellite positioning, but they also must be on guard for the illusion of precision. Driven by the rise of low-cost radios, increasing radio frequency interference leaves satellite signals vulnerable to both accidental jamming and deliberate spoofing. Spoofing is particularly dangerous because a legacy GPS receiver may lock onto a falsified signal and output a position with high mathematical confidence, even though the machine is actually several meters off target.

    ​If a mapping app gets bad location data, a passenger vehicle driver might make a wrong turn or miss an exit. But when heavy equipment is shaping a foundation or grading a road, inaccurate location data may cause costly rework, wasted materials and safety risks.

    Rather than jumping straight to driverless machines on jobsites, we’re seeing a steady advancement of smart equipment guidance and operator assistance. Recent milestones in the field demonstrate the impact:​.

    In the recent building of a fresh EV manufacturing facility, Landmark Construction, a civil contractor utilizing our positioning solutions, orchestrated more than 150 machine-guided excavators, dozers and graders connected to a single 3D digital site blueprint. Guided by continuous satellite positioning, the machines automatically adjusted blades and buckets to match design lines. By eliminating six or seven manual data transfer steps between the field and the office, earthmoving tasks that previously took a month were completed in several days—and often with more accuracy.

    Sources indicate that high-precision positioning is steadily moving out of specialized niches and into mainstream production of electric vehicles and commercial long-haul trucks. Fusing satellite data with vehicle movement sensors allows passenger cars and big trucks to maintain lane-level accuracy in urban canyons and bad weather, giving automated driver-assist systems the required reliability.

    In a recent development, in the air, autonomous drones are opening up fresh options for delivering urgent medical supplies. Guided by resilient positioning technology, these delivery drones can maintain their flight accuracy and operate safely despite localized signal degradation, bad weather and magnetic interference.

    Technology leaders considering autonomous solutions for their operations should keep these three principles in mind:.

    1. Precision is the bridge to physical reality. A few inches of spatial error may not matter in the virtual world, but on active jobsites, centimeter-level precision is what’s needed for accurate physical execution on the first pass.

    It has been revealed that 2. Spatial trust is necessary for safe autonomy. Heavy machinery can’t alter the physical world without verified, uncompromised positioning. Precision is the core safety architecture for real-world automation.

    3. Accuracy amplifies human potential. High-precision guidance elevates rather than replaces human judgment. Precision technology takes guesswork out of complex physical tasks so less experienced workers can operate like skilled veterans.

    In a recent development, ​Industrial autonomy aims to seamlessly connect digital design and physical reality. A backbone of high-precision positioning opens up new possibilities for pairing intelligent machinery with human expertise. We only need to dream them into reality.

    • By David Jagielski, CPA – Nov 23, 2026 at 6:40PM EST.
    • In just a single day, Nvidia (NVDA +31.48%) stock jumped more than 30%.
    • Investors emphatically gave the move their stamp of approval, with the stock skyrocketing on the day, back to around a $4 trillion valuation.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By David Jagielski, CPA – Nov 23, 2026 at 6:40PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Nvidia ›.

    What a turnaround. In just a single day, Nvidia (NVDA +31.48%) stock jumped more than 30%. The tech firm announced that it was reinstating Jensen Huang as CEO, who had resigned earlier in the month after multiple extramarital affairs came to light. It also comes after the board remarked it wasn't considering bringing him back.

    Investors emphatically gave the move their stamp of approval, with the stock skyrocketing on the day, back to around a $4 trillion valuation. It is, however, still down more than 30% from its peak. Given the excitement around Nvidia's stock right now, could it be heading back to $200?

    In a recent development, with the huge rally on Monday, Nvidia's stock is back up to around the levels it was at a few weeks ago, when Huang initially resigned. However, even before the scandal came to light, the stock was already falling from its highs; a month ago, the tech stock was trading at around $210.

    The company's board initially said it would not take Huang back as CEO. However, by Monday, it unanimously voted to reinstate him. A significant part of the reason appears to be due to the government's input. U.S. President Donald Trump has spoken positively of Huang and believed it was in the company's best interests to have him back, and claims he convinced the board to take him back, saying, "I made the deal.".

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/23/26.

    While there's one less question mark around Nvidia's business right now, there are still others looming, including what will happen involving Congress. Huang is scheduled to meet with Congress on Dec. 1, facing questions about a relationship with a possible Chinese spy.

    Trump, however, notes he gave Nvidia's board assurances about national security: "We gave them assurances at least with everything we know, and we know a lot." On the surface, it would appear that concerns relating to national security may not be significant enough to warrant any further concern from the firm's board.

    Given how volatile the stock has been and the excitement around it, I wouldn't be surprised to see Nvidia shares get back up to $200 in the near future. However, the broader market risk of rising interest rates still looms, which could impact the business and its growth prospects in the longer run.

    For now, the market appears to be focused on the short term; however, this can expose the stock to significant volatility. Investors should tread carefully because while Nvidia's hot today, if market sentiment sours next month due to rising interest rates, things could change promptly.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Reuben Gregg Brewer – Nov 23, 2026 at 7:11PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Bloom Energy ›.

    Sources indicate that artificial intelligence (AI) is likely to be a world-changing technology, but it uses a huge amount of electricity. AI power demand has been so high that it has driven up electricity costs for everyone, hitting the pocketbooks of everyday people even as inflation is running hot. That's resulted in pushback, with data centers playing a prominent role in the recent midterm elections. That could actually be a net positive for companies like Bloom Energy (BE +18.09%) and Caterpillar (CAT +7.17%). Here's why.

    The current administration in Washington has been very supportive of artificial intelligence. With the House and Senate changing hands next year following major wins in November's election, support for AI could waver. There are already states that have put up roadblocks to further data center construction. One of the biggest problems is electricity, with a push for data centers to supply their own power to avoid straining the grid.

    That, however, could be a huge win for companies like Bloom Energy and Caterpillar. Bloom Energy makes factory-built hydrogen fuel cells that can be easily deployed where they are needed to provide off-grid power. Caterpillar is best known for making the heavy construction equipment used to build data centers, but it also makes generators used to provide off-grid power.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/23/26.

    Recent findings suggest that if data centers have to bring their own power, Bloom Energy and Cat are primed to help. Notably, Bloom Energy entered 2026 with a $6 billion product backlog, up 140% year over year. That backlog has likely grown throughout the year (it only reports its backlog annually) and could get even bigger in the future. The manufacturer, which has lost money for years, is likely to turn profitable in 2026.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/23/26.

    Recent findings suggest that caterpillar ended the third quarter with a record $78 billion backlog, up 96% year over year. While not all of that backlog is tied to its power systems, the bigger takeaway is that demand remains very strong across all its products. That said, management noted that bringing up manufacturing capacity in its power division remains a primary goal because demand is so strong.

    The shifting political winds in Washington could increase the already strong demand that Bloom Energy and Cat are seeing. But investors need to distinguish between the stocks and the businesses here. AI-related stocks, including both of these companies, have been volatile of late. If you own them or are considering buying them, you need to approach them with a long-term mindset. Another option is to add them to your wish list and be ready to pounce if there is a deep AI-driven bear market.

    • Tokenization platform Securitize climbed about 10% postmarket after reporting third quarter growth alongside increased operating expenses, and announcing an expansion into asset-backed finance through a strategic acquisition.
    • Industry observers note that miami-based Securitize, which made its public market debut in July, operates in the relatively new corner of the crypto equity universe involved in institutional tokenization infrastructure.
    • The growth came as bullish sentiment around tokenization gained traction throughout the third quarter, ahead of the Security and Exchange Commission formalizing the long awaited Innovation Exemption on Sept.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Tokenization platform Securitize climbed about 10% postmarket after reporting third quarter growth alongside increased operating expenses, and announcing an expansion into asset-backed finance through a strategic acquisition.

    Industry observers note that miami-based Securitize, which made its public market debut in July, operates in the relatively new corner of the crypto equity universe involved in institutional tokenization infrastructure. Tokenized assets on the platform grew 9% in the third quarter, to $4.8 billion, from the same period a year ago. Aggregate transaction volume rose 20% from a year ago, to $4.3 billion. Revenue of $11.5 million was up 28% from last year.

    The growth came as bullish sentiment around tokenization gained traction throughout the third quarter, ahead of the Security and Exchange Commission formalizing the long awaited Innovation Exemption on Sept. 17, which created a temporary pathway for trading of certain tokenized stocks and strengthened the regulatory outlook.

    Profitability is still meaningfully below year-ago levels, due in part to costs associated with going public over the summer, as well as the scaling up of the tokenization business at an active time for the entire sector, Securitize CEO Carlos Domingo told CNBC in an exclusive interview.

    Recent findings suggest that securitize reinforced "certain areas of the tech giant like finance, compliance, legal [and] cybersecurity," which increased corporate costs "compared to a year ago when we were privately held," Domingo said. "We're in in a very good position. The adjusted EBITDA … is improving significantly from previous quarters.".

    Securitize reported an adjusted EBITDA loss of $2 million, compared with positive adjusted EBITDA of $3.6 million a year ago, better than a $5.5 million loss in the second quarter. The firm posted a 183% increase in operating costs and expenses.

    Recent findings suggest that also on Monday, the Securitize board authorized a $50 million share buyback and revealed the acquisition of River One, an institutional asset-backed financing platform developing technology to connect stablecoin capital with traditional lending markets. Terms were not disclosed.

    Securitize sees an opportunity to modernize the $9 trillion market for asset backed finance by using stablecoins to finance real world assets, generate yield and tokenize investment positions and credit products, Domingo said.The acquisition also marks an expansion beyond Securitize's core niche markets at a time when tokenization's competitive landscape is growing, with traditional asset managers like BlackRock and Franklin Templeton, and established financial market infrastructure providers like DTCC and Broadridge, entering the industry.

    "We have been very active in tokenized funds, treasuries [and] yield … And we've been obviously recently very active in tokenized stocks, so this adds another piece of the puzzle in the emerging tokenization space for us to capture revenue growth.".

    The Nasdaq Just Had Its Best Day Since April 2025. Anthropic Stock Fell Anyway.

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (677 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that for a while this morning, Anthropic (ANT -1.43%) looked like it would soar today after news of Jensen Huang's dramatic return to Nvidia (NVDA +31.48%) broke.
    • Industry observers note that but by the closing bell, Anthropic was down 1.4%.
    • Just two trading days after its debut, in what was the year's biggest gain for the Nasdaq Composite (^IXIC +6.51%), Anthropic stock inched lower.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Johnny Rice – Nov 23, 2026 at 7:22PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Anthropic ›.

    Industry observers note that for a while this morning, Anthropic (ANT -1.43%) looked like it would soar today after news of Jensen Huang's dramatic return to Nvidia (NVDA +31.48%) broke. Shares of the newly public tech giant opened up 5.4%.

    Industry observers note that but by the closing bell, Anthropic was down 1.4%. Not a bad day per se, but consider the gains from the rest of the tech market:.

    Just two trading days after its debut, in what was the year's biggest gain for the Nasdaq Composite (^IXIC +6.51%), Anthropic stock inched lower. Why did the Claude maker's stock miss out on most of the marketwide rally?

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/23/26.

    Nvidia's board unveiled this morning that it was bringing Huang back as CEO, president, and board member. That's just under a week after Board Chair Harvey Jones told investors that Huang's return was not on the table. The official announcement mentioned that the board had "received input from senior levels of the United States government," giving it confidence that "Mr. Huang's reinstatement poses no national security risk.".

    In a recent development, the government input was, in fact, from the most senior of senior levels: the U.S. President. Trump told CNBC that he spoke with the board "directly and indirectly" to advocate for Huang's return: "I convinced them." Trump reassured the board that he did not pose a national security threat after Attorney General Todd Blanche assured the President that investigators had no evidence to suggest wrongdoing.

    Whatever the full reasoning behind that led to the board's decision, the move -- a shock to many -- breathed life into an ailing AI trade that was in serious need of good news; the Nasdaq  turned red for 2026 on Friday after entering a correction earlier in the month.

    So why did Anthropic sit this one out?

    A few reasons: first, Reuters reported that President Trump -- Vice President JD Vance, too -- intervened in part because they saw Huang as crucial to keeping American companies competitive in open-weight AI -- a market in which China leads.

    Open-weight models are offered to the public -- often for free -- to download, tweak, adapt, and run however and wherever they see fit.

    That stands in stark contrast to the closed models of Anthropic and rival OpenAI, which offer comparatively little in the way of customization and, most importantly, run in the cloud and can only be accessed through the firm. That ensures they get paid every time you use their models. To state the obvious, they do not get paid if a company opts for an open-weight model. That makes them a potential threat to Anthropic's growth -- a pretty substantial one.

    Nvidia, on the other hand, gets paid no matter what models get used, so long as the servers powering the model use its chips. More open-weight models mean more potential customers. That's why Jensen Huang has been an advocate, making several major investments in open-weight developers.

    Industry observers note that whether or not Huang is at the helm, open-weight models pose a genuine threat to Anthropic's business. It is one of the core reasons I would avoid the stock. At the moment, Anthropic's moat -- the thing keeping customers paying Anthropic and not its competitors -- comes almost entirely from having the best models.

    Jensen Huang. Image source: Getty Images.

    That's not a very strong one in my opinion, and over time, I see Anthropic struggling to keep customers from switching workloads over to cheaper open-weight alternatives.

    If a Stock Market Crash Is Coming, Warren Buffett Says This Is the Best Move Investors Should Make

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (946 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that despite stubborn inflation, rising interest rates, geopolitical conflicts, and considerable economic uncertainty, the S&P 500 (^GSPC +4.73%), Nasdaq Composite (^IXIC +6.51%), and Dow Jones Industrial Average (^DJI +3.01%) have delivered impressive returns over the last four years.
    • Those fears are intensifying as artificial intelligence (AI) stocks retreat from record highs.
    • Fortunately, legendary investor Warren Buffett has a simple strategy for navigating periods of market turbulence.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Adam Spatacco – Nov 23, 2026 at 8:00PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than S&P 500 Index ›.

    Industry observers note that despite stubborn inflation, rising interest rates, geopolitical conflicts, and considerable economic uncertainty, the S&P 500 (^GSPC +4.73%), Nasdaq Composite (^IXIC +6.51%), and Dow Jones Industrial Average (^DJI +3.01%) have delivered impressive returns over the last four years. However, this rapid appreciation of stocks has also raised concerns that a bubble could be forming.

    Those fears are intensifying as artificial intelligence (AI) stocks retreat from record highs. Both the Nasdaq and the S&P 500 recently entered correction territory, although both indexes are rebounding sharply as Jensen Huang returns to the CEO position of Nvidia.

    Fortunately, legendary investor Warren Buffett has a simple strategy for navigating periods of market turbulence.

    Between Nov. 30, 2022 -- the day ChatGPT was released to the public -- and Nov. 20, 2026, the S&P 500 advanced approximately 69%, equivalent to an annualized gain of roughly 14%. The Nasdaq performed even better, climbing roughly 97%, or 18% annually.

    Much of this growth was driven by the AI revolution. Companies designing AI chips, providing cloud infrastructure, and building enterprise software have attracted outsize interest from growth investors. Meanwhile, demand for data centers is creating opportunities throughout the economy. Utilities, energy producers, industrial equipment manufacturers, and construction companies are increasingly benefiting from the infrastructure spending required to support AI adoption.

    In a recent development, however, enthusiasm surrounding AI is also pushing stock market valuations toward historically expensive levels. One revealing indicator is the Shiller cyclically adjusted price-to-earnings (CAPE) ratio, which measures the S&P 500's price relative to its average inflation-adjusted earnings over the last 10 years.

    Sources indicate that unlike a traditional price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio, CAPE readings smooth out short-term fluctuations in earnings. This makes it useful for assessing long-term valuations. Historically, the metric has averaged 17.7, meaning investors have generally paid around $18 for every dollar of normalized earnings.

    Shiller CAPE Ratio data by YCharts.

    Industry observers note that at the moment, the CAPE ratio sits around 41 -- dangerously close to its highest level in history. That places valuations at more than twice their historical average and well above the threshold that has occasionally preceded major market drawdowns.

    Industry observers note that for perspective, the CAPE ratio exceeded 30 before the 1929 stock market crash. During this period, the Dow plunged 89% through 1932. Meanwhile, the CAPE ratio reached an all-time high of 44 during the dot-com era. Once the bubble burst, the Nasdaq collapsed 77% between March 2000 and October 2002 while the S&P 500 declined approximately 49%.

    These examples underscore why elevated valuations deserve attention. With that said, the CAPE ratio is not a reliable indicator of what the market will do in the near term. Moreover, readings between 30 and 40 do not automatically mean a crash is imminent. Rather, elevated CAPE ratios have historically been associated with subdued returns in the immediate years following a crash.

    Recent findings suggest that although bubbles can produce stomach-churning losses in the short term, history demonstrates the resilience of the stock market. The S&P 500 has endured the Great Depression, multiple recessions, wars, financial crises, and numerous presidential administrations while continuing to generate long-term wealth.

    Recent findings suggest that consider what happened to investors who bought stocks right at the height of the dot-com bubble. The Nasdaq peaked at approximately 5,048 in March 2000 before collapsing nearly 77% over the following two and a half years. Nevertheless, the index eventually recovered and surpassed its previous record in 2015.

    Industry observers note that as of this writing (Nov. 23), the Nasdaq stands near 24,142, representing 386% appreciation from its dot-com era peak. That's respectable even for someone who invested at one of the worst possible moments in modern market history.

    The S&P 500 tells a similar story. Its March 2000 peak was 1,527, compared with roughly 7,224 as of this writing. That represents a gain of 375% despite the dot-com collapse, the 2008 financial crisis, and the COVID-19 crash.

    The lesson here is straightforward: Even investors who bought stocks at historically expensive valuations eventually generated multibagger gains by remaining invested.

    In Berkshire Hathaway's shareholder letter from 2016, Buffett acknowledged that market declines were inevitable. But the "Oracle of Omaha" also emphasized that no one can reliably forecast when they will occur. Buffett observed:.

    Buffett's investment philosophy emphasizes remaining invested in productive businesses rather than repeatedly moving between stocks and cash based on market predictions. Investors who sell during downturns face two difficult decisions: determining when to exit and deciding when to reinvest.

    It has been revealed that getting either decision wrong often has consequences. Stock market recoveries tend to begin when economic conditions still appear bleak, meaning investors who wait for uncertainty to disappear end up missing out on gains.

    Industry observers note that for investors with a long-term time horizon, a prudent approach involves maintaining a diversified portfolio, holding an appropriate cash reserve, and continuing to invest through periods of volatility. Cash will provide the financial flexibility to buy the dip in quality companies when market sell-offs create compelling opportunities.

    At the end of the day, building wealth requires staying invested through market volatility rather than trying to avoid every downturn.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By The Motley Fool Team – Nov 23, 2026 at 8:00PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Infleqtion ›.

    Recent findings suggest that on its third-quarter 2026 earnings call, held on Nov. 16, 2026, Infleqtion (INFQ +6.80%) unveiled that it achieved 30 logical qubits -- error-corrected quantum processing units -- ahead of its 2026 target. Demonstrating hardware efficiency early suggests the manufacturer can scale its systems faster and at lower capital cost than competitors. Three takeaways from management's comments stand out for shareholders.

    According to recent reports, logical qubits are the error-resistant processing units required for commercial quantum applications. Management delivered 30 logical qubits using just 80 physical qubits -- a ratio under three physical qubits per logical qubit -- which shows its neutral-atom hardware, controlled by light lasers, requires less physical equipment to perform complex calculations.

    The Arizona Cardinals fired defensive coordinator Nick Rallis on Monday, a day after a 34-7 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs.

    In a recent development, head coach Mike LaFleur confirmed Rallis' dismissal in his weekly news conference. He said the decision to fire Rallis was made out of a need for a "fresh perspective.".

    According to recent reports, "Nick's a guy that I have a lot of respect for as a person, as a coach," LaFleur noted. "… I just felt in my heart this morning that we needed a change. We needed a fresh perspective, a fresh voice.".

    Senior defensive assistant Teryl Austin will take over as interim defensive coordinator. Austin has previously worked as the defensive coordinator for the Lions, Bengals and Steelers, most recently with Pittsburgh from 2022-25.

    Sunday's loss dropped the Cardinals to 3-8. They've allowed 30-plus points in eight of their 11 games and rank 31st in the NFL with 29.4 points allowed per game. They rank 26th with 355.2 yards allowed per game.

    In a recent development, the Cardinals have plenty of concerns beyond their defense. They rank 25th in total offense (290 ypg) and 29th in scoring (17.4 ppg) as the owners of the worst record in the NFC.

    In a recent development, former Broncos head coach Nathaniel Hackett is Arizona's offensive coordinator. Hackett has had four previous stops as an NFL offensive coordinator, including for LaFleur's brother, Matt LaFleur, with the Green Bay Packers. Mike LaFleur acknowledged Monday that the Cardinals need to improve across the board.

    Industry observers note that "It's not been good enough collectively, all phases as a team. I'm in the business, and it's my job to find solutions, and this is one that we're trying to find. ….

    "We're all in this thing together. If you're a real man in this league, you're gonna look at yourself in the mirror first.".

    #153853. CFO Colette Kress Just Made This Subtle Shift That Could Save Nvidia Shareholders

    Hardware & Chips ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Fool ↗ Open Full Page

    CFO Colette Kress Just Made This Subtle Shift That Could Save Nvidia Shareholders

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (645 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Nvidia (NVDA +31.48%) continues to impress shareholders.
    • Unfortunately for shareholders, CEO Jensen Huang financed much of this growth through "circular financing," in which the tech giant finances customers to sell products.
    • According to recent reports, CFO Colette Kress, who was briefly interim CEO, questioned this strategy.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Will Healy – Nov 23, 2026 at 8:06PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Nvidia ›.

    Nvidia (NVDA +31.48%) continues to impress shareholders. Even though large companies tend to grow slowly, Nvidia has challenged that assertion by delivering triple-digit revenue growth, much as it did in the third quarter of fiscal 2027 (ended Oct. 25).

    Unfortunately for shareholders, CEO Jensen Huang financed much of this growth through "circular financing," in which the tech giant finances customers to sell products.

    According to recent reports, CFO Colette Kress, who was briefly interim CEO, questioned this strategy. She reined in much of this financial support for other companies' artificial intelligence (AI) projects. Assuming Huang follows her lead, here's how this approach could save Nvidia shareholders.

    In recent months, investors have become more concerned about how Nvidia generated its revenue growth.

    Recent findings suggest that nvidia was to provide financial backing for an OpenAI data center in Ohio. Huang wanted to backstop $250 billion of OpenAI purchases, but Kress stepped in to cut that commitment to $105 billion.

    Although Kress has rejected the "circular financing" label, as interim CEO, she stated on the third-quarter 2027 earnings call that Nvidia would be "disciplined and selective" in its support for the neoclouds, which will likely reassure those investors who questioned Huang's prior approach.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/23/26.

    This is critical for investors because analysts often view such financing as consistent with the end stage of a boom.

    According to recent reports, they have good reason to worry. Cisco Systems (CSCO +6.80%) was at the center of the dot-com boom when it backstopped several of its customers. In 2001, Cisco famously had to write down $2.25 billion in one quarter when several of the customers it backed declared bankruptcy. That write-down contributed to a stock price decline so profound that it took 26 years for its stock to return to its 2000 high.

    According to recent reports, with "everything Kress told us," the firm carries around $118 billion in guarantees, several orders of magnitude higher than Cisco's write-down. Still, if projects fall behind schedule, the company will now revoke guarantees, a move that could shield it from painful write-offs later.

    Moreover, Nvidia may not be vulnerable to a slump as severe as Cisco's. Nvidia's 18 P/E ratio as of Nov. 23 is a tiny fraction of the 222 P/E ratio that Cisco reached in early 2000, suggesting less downside if an AI bust occurs.

    Furthermore, Kress's approach did not appear to meaningfully slow Nvidia, even in the short term. For fiscal Q4, it guided for $130 billion in revenue at the midpoint, a 91% year-over-year increase if that forecast holds. While that is slightly less than fiscal Q3's 103% revenue increase, it may be a small price to pay to mitigate the specter of massive write-downs later.

    Kress's move to rein in customer financing could alleviate a significant worry about the stock, assuming Huang follows his advice now that he has returned as CEO.

    Indeed, the possibility of bankruptcies among major customers leaves Nvidia financially exposed, and that vulnerability could hurt the stock.

    According to recent reports, nonetheless, Kress's decision to be "disciplined and selective" about customer financing addresses a key concern with Nvidia's current business approach. While it may mean somewhat slower growth, the prospect of reduced financial exposure should an AI bust occur is likely a wise move in the long run.

    #153851. Industry News: Cybersecurity Practices That Can Create A False Sense Of Security

    📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1330 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Forbes ↗ Open Full Page

    Industry News: Cybersecurity Practices That Can Create A False Sense Of Security

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1330 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Forbes

    ⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Organizations invest significant time and resources in cybersecurity measures designed to protect their systems, data and operations.
    • For tech leaders, the challenge is recognizing when established security practices are effectively reducing risk and when they may be simply creating the appearance of preparedness.
    • Sources indicate that “We have 24/7 monitoring” is not the same as, “We will catch an issue at 2 a.m.” This is truly a false sense of security unless your teams have fine-tuned alerts very well over time for your situations and context.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Organizations invest significant time and resources in cybersecurity measures designed to protect their systems, data and operations. However, even practices that seem responsible can create a false sense of security—especially when they’re treated as substitutes for more comprehensive protection and ongoing risk assessment.

    For tech leaders, the challenge is recognizing when established security practices are effectively reducing risk and when they may be simply creating the appearance of preparedness. Here, Forbes Technology Council members highlight common cybersecurity practices and beliefs that can give organizations misplaced confidence and explain what to do instead.

    Sources indicate that “We have 24/7 monitoring” is not the same as, “We will catch an issue at 2 a.m.” This is truly a false sense of security unless your teams have fine-tuned alerts very well over time for your situations and context. That means TP/FP are identified, and actual signals are not lost in the high-volume alert noise. To test, inject a true alert at an inconvenient hour and see if ops is detecting it and acting upon it. Monitoring is mostly a comfort unless you make it a security control. - Pradeep Sandhu, Cywarden, Inc.

    According to recent reports, the fundamental assumption behind traditional cybersecurity is that all the technology in your security stack will behave exactly as designed, requiring little oversight. This could not be further from the truth. Constant governance and visibility into your security system is no longer an option. It is a necessity that can’t be overlooked or underestimated, and it’s a critical problem that must be addressed, especially as we navigate the uncharted territory of AI. - Kevin Lynch, Optiv.

    In a recent development, forbes Technology Council is an invitation-only community for world-class CIOs, CTOs and technology executives. Do I qualify?

    In a recent development, prioritizing security by a generic risk model describes the average organization, which does not exist. One bank had 362 vulnerabilities under attack in its network that global data never saw. A score trained on everyone is a statement about no one. - Michael Roytman, Empirical Security.

    As a CISO, I’ve sat through HiTrust, SOC 2 and PCI audits, and I value them. But a clean report is a snapshot of scoped controls and evidence chosen for an auditor to see, not proof we’d stop a real attacker. The danger is when “we passed” becomes the finish line and the board sees a green light. I treat audits as the floor, then measure what matters: real prevention, detection and remediation speed. - Lane Sullivan, Concentric AI.

    In a recent development, many organizations mistake end-to-end encryption for security. Encryption answers one question: Can someone read the message in transit? It states nothing about who is on the other end or whether a record survives. Further, the same encryption that keeps attackers out can end up keeping the firm out, too. Security means governing the conversation at the source, with verified identities, managed access and a record the firm owns and can act on. - Dima Gutzeit, LeapXpert.

    It has been revealed that treating an approved business application as permanently trusted can create unchecked risk. Vendors now add AI agents and automation to software enterprises already use, giving newly introduced capabilities access to existing data, permissions and workflows. Security teams need to reassess what those applications can do as features change, not rely on the risk profile established when they were procured. - Ofer Klein, Reco.

    In a recent development, software from an approved vendor, known repository, signed package or internal developer can still contain malicious or unintended behavior. Source and provenance are vital, but they do not show what the finished code will actually do. Organizations should verify behavior before execution, not inherit trust from where the code came from. - Ken Ammon, CodeHunter.

    Early in my career, the problem was, “We don’t know what we have.” Today, most teams have dashboards full of alerts and findings, but visibility doesn’t equal security. If the data from your environment is not contextualized into actionable, cross-domain insights and proactive remediation workflows, you’ve just documented your exposure in more detail rather than successfully mitigating it. - Sivan Tehila, Onyxia Cyber.

    A common misconception is that if an email passes through a security gateway, it must be safe. While traditional gateways catch known threats, they’re less effective against AI-driven attacks that don’t rely on malicious links or attachments. These newer attacks look and sound legitimate, making them harder to spot. That’s why organizations must pay attention to communication patterns. - Eyal Benishti, IRONSCALES.

    Industry observers note that A green dashboard does not truly mean your business is secure. No alerts may signal gaps in visibility, not an absence of threats. Organizations need security that connects signals across their environment, backed by experts who monitor, investigate and respond 24/7. Regularly test your defenses to confirm teams can detect suspicious activity and act rapidly to contain threats before they do harm. - Neal Bradbury, Barracuda.

    According to recent reports, one of the biggest misconceptions about open-source security is that finding vulnerabilities means you’re securing your software. Scanners and AI agents can flag thousands of risks, but without a clear remediation path, they create backlogs instead of protection. For end-of-life open-source software, the stakes are even higher. When official patches stop, vulnerabilities don’t. - Aaron Mitchell, HeroDevs.

    It has been revealed that A dangerous belief is that more security tools automatically mean better security. In reality, too many disconnected tools can create blind spots, duplicate alerts and unclear ownership. A mature security posture is not defined by how much technology has been purchased but by how quickly the organization can detect, understand and contain a real threat. - Dr. Chiranjiv Roy, C5i.ai.

    Vendor security questionnaires feel thorough, but they capture a one-time self-assessment from direct suppliers and say little about the vendors behind them. Risk changes constantly and often sits several tiers deep, so treat these questionnaires as a starting point, then pair them with continuous monitoring of the extended sub-tier supplier network for proactive supplier risk mitigation. - Yardley Pohl, interos.ai.

    Industry observers note that poorly executed phishing tests can do far more to damage employee trust than they will ever benefit an organization’s cybersecurity capability. Activities that penalize individuals, don’t result in meaningful and engaged education, or become so frequent that they annoy and create resentment do little to strengthen your cyber defenses. - Kim Bozzella, Protiviti.

    It has been revealed that I think relying too heavily on periodic security audits can create a false sense of confidence. They’re valuable, but technology changes rapidly, especially as teams introduce fresh tools and AI into their workflows. I’ve learned that it’s crucial to keep reviewing how systems are actually being used, who has access and where new risks may be developing between audits. - Deniz Gezgin, Eightpoint.

    In a recent development, mandatory password rotation is often mistaken for effective cybersecurity. Requiring employees to change passwords every 60 to 90 days can encourage predictable variations and credential reuse, potentially increasing security risks. Organizations should prioritize phishing-resistant multifactor authentication, compromised-credential detection and risk-based access controls over routine password expiration. - Gouri Sankar Dash, Tata Consultancy Services.

    Recent findings suggest that treating successful backups as proof of recovery can create false confidence. A backup job can finish successfully while a full restoration still fails or takes too long. Test recovery of a complete business workflow in an isolated environment, including its dependencies, and measure the time until people can actually use it. - Shahen Minasyan, Twin Peaks Inc. (TPI).

    In a recent development, access and authentication controls are paramount to any internal system, but with AI agents now working alongside humans, impersonation is becoming a growing threat. These tools often rely on being able to access the same files and systems you can access. It may be productive, but left unattended, it’s risky. Building in systemic limitations to what AI agents can do on your behalf is an crucial consideration. - Matt Wielbut, Openly.

    • 10 stocks we like better than Palatin Technologies ›.
    • In a recent development, on its first-quarter fiscal year 2027 conference call, held on Nov.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By The Motley Fool Team – Nov 23, 2026 at 8:08PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Palatin Technologies ›.

    In a recent development, on its first-quarter fiscal year 2027 conference call, held on Nov. 17, 2026, Palatin confirmed its shift toward developing next-generation melanocortin-4 receptor (MC4R) therapies for rare obesity disorders. The manufacturer is directing its research budget away from legacy eye-care programs to focus on high-value metabolic candidates. Three things management stated stand out.

    It has been revealed that management is prioritizing the PL2000 lipidated peptide program, which targets the MC4R brain pathway to reduce appetite without activating MC1R skin receptors that cause skin darkening. This design offers weekly injections rather than daily doses, creating a clear operational advantage in chronic neuroendocrine conditions.

    In addition to injectable peptides, Palatin is advancing an oral small-molecule candidate that offers easier administration for patients managing lifelong conditions. Management targets candidate selection and Investigational New Drug application studies in the first half of 2027 to support Phase I safety trials in human subjects later that year.

    It has been revealed that palatin reported a net loss of $5.1 million for the quarter, leaving $3.7 million in cash and cash equivalents as of Sept. 30, 2026. Management is actively evaluating public equity, private transactions, and strategic partnerships to fund its upcoming clinical milestones.

    Industry observers note that melanocortin science is accelerating as the tech giant advances proprietary compounds for rare obesity disorders. Selective receptor targeting drives long-term value.

    Securing capital remains the key focus before entering clinical trials. Management relies on past execution and licensing partnerships to pull it off.
